items.summary: The planned US$5.5 billion IPO of Nvidia-backed Firmus Grid was withdrawn after failing to attract sufficient support for its A$11 share price. The cancellation highlights growing investor caution regarding high valuations and capital demands in the AI infrastructure sector. While Firmus targets a US$30 billion valuation based on a pipeline of 912MW, only 46MW is currently built. Concerns include the company's lack of a proven track record, reliance on a few major customers, and the risk of shareholder selling. Other investors, such as UniSuper, declined to participate due to the valuation, noting that much must go right to justify the price. The event underscores broader skepticism about AI funding as borrowing costs rise.
items.title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus IPO Cancelled Amid AI Funding Concerns

items.summary: The Financial Times reported that OpenAI's annualised revenue is approximately US$20 billion less than previously signalled, based on financial documents shared with investors. The report notes a discrepancy between OpenAI's figures and those reported by media outlets, attributing the difference to how investors calculated comparisons with rival Anthropic. Reuters could not independently verify the report, and OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
items.title: Report Says OpenAI Revenue Lower Than Expected

items.summary: OpenAI disclosed a $20bn reduction in projected annual revenue, citing a revised $50bn forecast compared to a previous $70bn signal. This adjustment, attributed to measurement differences with rival Anthropic, raised concerns about AI demand growth. The news triggered declines in tech stocks, including Nvidia and Oracle, while OpenAI continues early-stage talks for a $30bn funding round.
items.title: OpenAI Cuts Revenue Projection by $20bn Amid AI Growth Questions

items.summary: Citrix warns administrators to immediately patch NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances against CVE-2026-107406, a critical flaw allowing remote code execution or denial-of-service. The vulnerability requires specific SAML configurations. While Citrix reports no known unmitigated exploits, it urges affected customers to upgrade to recommended versions. Shadowserver notes over 21,000 exposed NetScaler IP addresses, though the number of vulnerable instances remains unknown.
items.title: Citrix Urges Immediate Patching for Critical NetScaler Vulnerability

items.summary: The EU is reportedly close to striking a deal to loosen electric vehicle regulations for the third time in two years. France and Germany have agreed to reduce emissions targets from 90% to 80%, a move that could allow automakers to continue producing polluting vehicles after 2035. Critics argue these rollbacks undermine climate goals and favor Chinese EVs, which are gaining market share. The proposal faces opposition from six other EU countries, but France's shift in stance may secure enough votes to pass the changes. This decision comes amid ongoing climate crises and rising oil prices.
items.title: EU May Loosen EV Rules Again as France and Germany Seek Deal

items.summary: Around 100 Baltimore residents gathered to urge the Maryland Department of the Environment to deny an air permit renewal for the WIN Waste trash incinerator. While state regulators announced the shutdown of a medical-waste incinerator due to illegal pollution, Baltimore County approved a contract allowing WIN Waste to continue operating for up to 10 more years. Residents cite health risks from emissions and ash, noting a recent study estimated $54 million in annual health damages. WIN Waste officials claim a $45 million upgrade reduced emissions and that ash is non-hazardous. Community leaders dispute these claims, highlighting unresolved issues with independent ash testing and contrasting the county's new agreement with the state's recent enforcement action.
items.title: Baltimore Residents Protest Contradictory Incinerator Decisions

items.summary: SAJ Electric is strengthening its global brand image by focusing on channel partners and installers to demonstrate long-term commitment rather than competing solely on price. The company recently signed tennis player Alex de Minaur as a global ambassador and collaborates with distributors like OSW and Tradezone. Through certifications, extended warranties, and technical support, SAJ Electric aims to shift its perception from a low-cost manufacturer to a trusted global brand.
items.title: SAJ Electric Builds Global Brand Image Through Strategic Partnerships and Long-Term Investment

items.summary: The UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero granted consent for the Green Hill Solar Farm in Northamptonshire and Milton Keynes. Developer Island Green Power will proceed with a 500 MW solar array and equivalent battery storage. The project includes biodiversity net gain, green corridors, and a community fund. Baroness Curran announced the decision following a six-month examination process.
items.title: UK approves 500 MW Green Hill solar and BESS project

items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced a CAD 2 billion investment to deliver 1 million home retrofits, including a national heat pump rebate for up to 820,000 households. Eligible low-income households receive up to CAD 10,000, while others get CAD 2,000. The program aims to cut emissions by more than 25 megatonnes.
items.title: Canada Announces Heat Pump Rebates and Home Retrofit Investment

items.summary: Louisiana's offshore wind industry is preparing to preserve its expertise and supply chain until January 21, 2029, anticipating a policy shift after President Donald Trump leaves office. The Trump administration halted development by paying developers roughly $4 billion to abandon projects, including 12 leases representing 21 gigawatts of potential capacity. While the industry faced a near standstill, Louisiana firms continued building on the East Coast, with Gulf-based firms receiving about $1 billion in investments by 2024. Industry leaders express hope that the current hostile environment will change, allowing the sector to revive under the next administration.
items.title: Louisiana Offshore Wind Industry Plans for Survival After 2029

items.summary: Amazon India has introduced a new Price History feature to help shoppers verify discount authenticity during the Great Indian Festival Sale. Users can compare current prices with historical data from one month, three months, or one year ago to determine the actual discount offered.
items.title: Amazon launches Price History feature to verify discount authenticity during sales

items.summary: Nikkei Asia reports that Apple has reduced production orders for iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max components due to dampened consumer demand and rising chip costs. Component orders for October were slashed by at least 15 percent. Reuters could not immediately verify the report, and Apple did not respond to a request for comment. The report notes that tech companies are scooping up chip capacity for AI data centers, sparking shortages.
items.title: Apple Cuts iPhone 18 Pro Orders Amid Soft Demand

items.summary: Meta announced an immediate ban on advertisements from ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok, in the United States, Japan, Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam. A spokesperson stated that declining promotional services to a competitor is a normal business practice. The move escalates the long-running rivalry between the two companies, which compete for user engagement and advertising dollars. TikTok did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
items.title: Meta Bans TikTok Ads in US and Other Countries

items.summary: Shobi Khan, CEO of Canary Wharf Group, credits a multi-pronged strategy for reversing the district's decline following Brexit and the pandemic. Since taking over in 2019, Khan has diversified the estate beyond financial services, increased residential and retail options, and improved transport access via the Elizabeth line. In 2026, the group reported record rental rates and over 92% office occupancy. Major tenants like Visa, Barclays, and Citi have committed significant space and capital, while visitor numbers are projected to exceed 76 million. Khan aims to replicate this success model in other markets.
items.title: Shobi Khan Revitalizes Canary Wharf with New Tenants and Amenities

items.summary: Everton owners The Friedkin Group are exploring the sale of the club less than two years after taking control in 2024. While TFG states the time is right to consider the next chapter following stability and stadium investment, the move has shocked fans and analysts. Criticism focuses on the group's perceived absenteeism, highlighted by manager David Moyes' lack of contact with chairman Dan Friedkin, and controversial player sales. Former goalkeeper Rachel Brown-Finnis acknowledged the club's improved financial footing but expressed hope that new owners will drive the club forward, noting the turbulent era fans endured.
items.title: Everton Owners Explore Club Sale Amidst Scrutiny

items.summary: Oil prices dropped after US President Donald Trump pledged to pause attacks on Iran until November 3rd midterm elections. China also resumed fuel exports. These developments offset concerns about supply disruptions from Hurricane Isaias in the Gulf of Mexico.
items.title: Oil prices fall as Trump pauses Iran attacks and China resumes fuel exports

items.summary: Anthropic updated its usage policy to prohibit sustained abusive or cruel behavior toward its Claude AI system. The policy relies on the model's ability to end interactions as the primary enforcement mechanism. While the update does not explicitly cite model welfare, Anthropic executives have previously discussed the concept of AI consciousness. The change reflects a growing philosophical debate regarding whether AI systems can be conscious and deserve protection.
items.title: Anthropic Updates Policy to Prevent Cruel Treatment of AI Models Amid Consciousness Debate

items.summary: Elon Musk questioned whether billionaire Mukesh Ambani is the 'real boss of India' as Starlink faces delays in securing final government approval to launch in the country. Musk accused unnamed powerful business interests of blocking the service, singling out Ambani whose Reliance conglomerate owns Jio. India's Ministry of Communications rejected these allegations, stating its rules are fair and that Starlink, along with other operators, awaits security clearances and spectrum allocation. Ambani and Reliance Group have not responded to the remarks. The BBC has reached out to both Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel for comment regarding the situation.
items.title: Elon Musk Questions Mukesh Ambani's Influence Over Starlink Delays in India

items.summary: Chinese astronomers using the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope (FAST) discovered a rare triple-star system named J0435+3233. The system includes a pulsar, a white dwarf, and a third star similar to the Sun. Published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, the findings help study stellar evolution and gravity theories. The third star explains the pulsar's unusual spin increase.
items.title: Chinese Astronomers Discover Rare Evolving Triple-Star System with FAST Telescope

items.summary: A team of Chinese women from the Miao ethnic minority in Guizhou has introduced a unique version of basketball to young athletes in Las Vegas. Played while wearing traditional ethnic clothing, this adaptation originated as a village sport in rural China. American players described the experience as delightful and sparked curiosity regarding the diversity of Chinese culture. The group, consisting of mothers and village women, is teaching this creative twist on the sport to the youth.
items.title: Chinese Miao Women Adapt Basketball for American Youth in Las Vegas

items.summary: Three years ago, Xi Jinping introduced Xi Jinping Thought on Culture at a national meeting in Beijing, stressing the need for stronger cultural confidence. He has since spoken on Chinese culture, underscoring the development of socialist culture to guide theories, unite people, and inspire them. The remarks highlight the importance of influencing the world through cultural strength.
items.title: Xi Jinping Emphasizes Cultural Confidence and Socialist Culture Development

items.summary: As Asia's economic landscape fragments, Hong Kong is exploring a shift from its traditional role as a gateway to becoming a financial connector for the region. Experts Mari Pangestu and Professor Edward K Y Chen argue that resilience requires regional cooperation rather than isolation. With the upcoming APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting, Hong Kong aims to facilitate capital flow and risk management between the Greater Bay Area, ASEAN, and the wider Asia-Pacific. The city seeks to support Chinese companies investing abroad through sustainable finance and green bonds, positioning itself within an interconnected regional economy rather than competing with other financial centers. This strategic pivot aims to maintain economic openness while addressing geopolitical uncertainty.
items.title: Hong Kong Seeks New Role as Asia-Pacific Capital Connector Amid Fragmentation

items.summary: The People's Bank of China stated that the RMB exchange rate operates under a managed floating regime driven by market forces and a basket of currencies. The central bank emphasized that market dynamics, rather than government intervention, determine the rate. It rejected claims of competitive devaluation, noting the currency has floated in both directions since 2010. China plans to expand domestic demand and deepen opening up during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30).
items.title: PBOC Confirms Market-Driven RMB Exchange Rate Policy Amid Global Discussions

items.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to South African jurist Navanethem "Navi" Pillay. Chair Jørgen Watne Frydnes cited her exceptional courage and integrity in leading toward a comprehensive global legal order and prosecuting war crimes. Simultaneously, the Nobel Foundation announced a prize increase to SEK 12 million to mark the 125th anniversary.
items.title: Navi Pillay Wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for Legal Order Work

items.summary: 7-Eleven Inc is considering moving parts of its US supply chain in-house to cut costs as inflation dampens consumer demand. CEO Mauricio Leyva and Seven & i Holdings CEO Stephen Dacus stated the company is exploring cost-cutting measures and developing in-house capabilities, noting that sentiment shows disposable income is being hit across the board.
items.title: 7-Eleven US Considers In-House Supply Chain Shift Amid Inflation

items.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Peace Prize to Navanethem Pillay for advancing international law and prosecuting war crimes. Chair Jørgen Watne Frydnes highlighted her role in strengthening global legal frameworks amidst rising political pressure.
items.title: Norwegian Nobel Committee announces 2026 Peace Prize winner Navanethem Pillay

items.summary: Japan's health ministry reported a record number of workers' compensation approvals for mental health disorders in fiscal 2025. The figure, 1,082 cases, marked a seventh consecutive year of highs. Among these, 76 involved suicide or attempted suicide, highlighting the impact of excessive workloads and psychological stress under legislation enacted in 2014.
items.title: Japan Records Surge in Mental Health Workers' Compensation Approvals

items.summary: Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her contributions to international law, announced by the Nobel jury in Oslo. The Norwegian Nobel Committee Chair noted her efforts to promote peace. The committee emphasized that resolving conflicts depends on the rule of law, especially as conflicts rise and legal institutions face attacks. The award carries 12 million Swedish kronor.
items.title: Navanethem Pillay Wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for International Law Work

items.summary: Several Japanese travel companies reported potential data breaches following cyberattacks. Skyticket faces risk to up to 14.64 million records, while H.I.S. may have leaked passport data for 627 people. Temairazu also confirmed unauthorized access to its systems.
items.title: Japanese Travel Companies Report Potential Data Breaches Affecting Millions

items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen stated on Friday that it destroyed three Houthi missile launch platforms used to threaten regional security. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki warned that attacks on civilians and infrastructure would receive a firm response. The announcement comes as fighting resumed in July after a 2022 truce, with the coalition launching the Dawn of Yemen operation to retake territory held by the group.
items.title: Saudi-led Coalition Claims Destruction of Houthi Missile Platforms in Yemen

items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canadians will determine the country's future, responding to Elon Musk's comments supporting the separation of Quebec, Alberta, and Saskatchewan. Carney emphasized that discussions should remain free from interference by foreign governments or large tech firms. Meanwhile, Alberta Premier Danielle Smith noted that separatist sentiment has weakened, while Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe responded to Musk with a single 'No.'
items.title: Carney Rejects Musk Separatism Remarks as Canadians Decide Future

items.summary: French S&D MEP Emma Rafowicz criticized Emmanuel Macron's government for handling student protests in France. She described the government's actions as completely irresponsible and argued that most violence stems from the police side. Rafowicz also accused the government of hoping protests would end during holidays and described French schools as being in shambles due to falling ceilings and poor food quality, citing this as a disrespect for young people.
items.title: French MEP Criticizes Macron Government Over Student Protests and School Conditions

items.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced that XXX has won this year's Nobel Peace Prize. The committee stated the recipient's name but noted that audio details regarding the award would be available later today.
items.title: Norwegian Nobel Committee Announces Winner of This Year's Peace Prize

items.summary: The Islamic Community of Bosnia and Herzegovina is selecting a new Grand Mufti, or Reis-ul-ulema, following the end of Husein Kavazovic's tenure. Three candidates are competing: Salem Dedovic, Nedzad Grabus, and Mensur Malkic. Their platforms differ, with Dedovic emphasizing political engagement, Grabus focusing on globalization, and Malkic prioritizing institutional strengthening. Imam Benjamin Idriz and Zenahir Mrakovic highlight the election's significance for European Muslims, noting the office's unique role. The new leader will face challenges including foreign influence attempts, rising Islamophobia, and fragile statehood, expected to engage actively in European debates on Islam while upholding democratic values.
items.title: New Grand Mufti Elected in Bosnia and Herzegovina Amid Regional Tensions

items.summary: Russia faces international concern over a pneumonic plague outbreak following the death of a laboratory worker in Siberia on October 2, 2026. Authorities have quarantined dozens of people and conducted nearly 5,000 tests, releasing 90% of those isolated. While Russian officials state there is no epidemic risk, the World Health Organisation notes insufficient information to fully assess the situation.
items.title: Russia investigates pneumonic plague outbreak after lab worker death

items.summary: Ethiopian drone strikes targeted Eritrean forces near Adigrat, according to a conflict monitor and witnesses. The attacks occurred as Eritrean troops were positioned in the area, raising fears of a wider regional war. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing rebels, while Eritrea claims Ethiopia seeks to invade. Diplomatic ties between the two nations were severed recently, and neither side has responded to questions about the fighting.
items.title: Ethiopian Drones Strike Eritrean Forces Near Adigrat Amid Regional Tensions

items.summary: Russian strikes on eastern Ukraine killed at least 33 people and injured 18, including an attack on a public bus. Authorities halted transport in Kramatorsk and Sloviansk due to security deterioration. President Zelenskyy warned of likely escalation as winter approaches and appealed for NATO defense support. Separate attacks in Kyiv and Pryluky also caused casualties.
items.title: Russian Strikes Kill 33 in Ukraine as Winter Attacks Intensify

items.summary: A coronial inquest heard that Noel Morris, a person of interest in the disappearance of Marilyn Wallman, was working at the Goonyella coalmine on March 21, 1972. Barry Morris, Noel's uncle, stated he saw Noel at the mine approximately 145 kilometres from where Marilyn disappeared. Meanwhile, Noel's wife Ann Morris was in Mackay giving birth to their daughter Jodie five days prior.
items.title: Alibi Presented for Person of Interest in 1972 Schoolgirl Disappearance

items.summary: Finland, once the world's happiest nation, confronts a severe debt crisis with national debt reaching 90.3% of GDP. The State Treasury projects a fiscal deficit of 4.2% of GDP in 2026, prompting EU scrutiny. While the government aims to save €9 billion, economists warn deeper cuts are needed. High unemployment, particularly among youth, and rising energy costs exacerbate the situation. Despite these challenges, Finland's export sector remains strong, and markets view its debt as relatively safe. However, the path forward involves difficult choices between spending cuts and potential tax hikes.
items.title: Finland Faces Debt Crisis Amid Austerity and Defense Spending

items.summary: Guinea-Bissau has adopted a new constitution that significantly strengthens the powers of the president at the expense of the prime minister and the government. Approved by 70% of voters in a referendum held on August 30, 2026, the reform was conducted under a military junta following a November 2025 coup. The new text grants the president expanded authority to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and to chair the Council of Ministers. Proponents argue this clarifies executive responsibilities and ends chronic power conflicts. However, the opposition and the PAIGC party criticize the process as illegitimate and fear it concentrates executive power. The constitution also bans amendments for ten years to prevent future power shifts. A presidential election is scheduled for December 6.
items.title: Guinea-Bissau's New Constitution Strengthens Presidential Powers Amidst Political Instability

items.summary: The Indian government has forwarded the name of Sudhakar Dalela, a senior career officer, as Ambassador to Nepal, signaling the importance of the India-Nepal relationship. Sources confirmed to The Hindu that the proposal was forwarded on October 6, 2026, and is expected to be approved soon by the Balen Shah government. This move suggests a shift towards favoring diplomatic experience over political flair, following concerns that a professional diplomat might not handle the unorthodox new Nepal Prime Minister, Balen Shah, effectively. Dalela, a 1993-batch officer with extensive experience in the region, replaces the previous political appointee trend.
items.title: India sends senior career officer Sudhakar Dalela as Nepal ambassador

items.summary: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council approved changes to export rules on Thursday to simplify tax refunds and reduce compliance disputes for Indian IT firms and global capability centres. The decisions expand benefits to services supplied through overseas branches and certain activities on foreign-owned goods. Industry association Nasscom welcomed the move, noting it could reduce litigation and working capital pressures.
items.title: GST Council Eases Export Rules For IT Firms, GCCs; TCS, Infosys, Wipro To Benefit From Faster Tax Refunds

items.summary: Telangana BJP State President N Ramchander Rao accused Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi of endorsing foreign critics like Elon Musk and Donald Trump while remaining silent against them. Rao alleged Gandhi supports views anti-India, specifically citing Musk's comments on Starlink. The remarks follow Musk calling Starlink's entry into India 'troubling' and Gandhi's subsequent reply on X.
items.title: Telangana BJP President Accuses Rahul Gandhi of Supporting Foreign Critics

items.summary: Hexaware Technologies shares jumped 10% in Friday's morning session after the company announced a multi-year partnership with AI developer Anthropic. The agreement involves integrating Anthropic's Claude model into Hexaware's enterprise platforms, Zerovity and AgentVerse. Siddharth Dhar, Hexaware's President of AI, stated the collaboration aims to help customers move AI solutions into production more quickly while maintaining predictable costs.
items.title: Hexaware Shares Surge Following Anthropic AI Partnership Announcement

items.summary: OpenAI stated it fired three researchers last week after an investigation found they violated policies on handling sensitive information. The dismissed researchers, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni, published a letter expressing concern over the termination process. OpenAI asserted the dismissals were not related to raising safety concerns, noting that such debates are encouraged. The researchers argued the firing could create uncertainty among remaining employees.
items.title: OpenAI Terminates Three Researchers Over Sensitive Information Violations

items.summary: Shobhit Mathur, co-founder of Rishihood University, defended the role of skilled foreign workers in the US tech industry. Recalling his time at Amazon, Mathur stated that approximately 100 H-1B visa holders were part of the initial team that built Amazon Web Services (AWS). He argued that these professionals contributed significantly to the company's transformation from a loss-making entity to a major profit generator. Mathur's comments follow renewed scrutiny of employment-based immigration, including the suspension of PERM labour certification for several major technology firms by the Trump administration in October 2026.
items.title: Ex-Amazon Executive Defends H-1B Workers Amid US Green-Card Restrictions

items.summary: Tata Consultancy Services shares rose over 4% following second-quarter results. While Goldman Sachs and Nomura maintained Buy ratings with targets of ₹2,210 and ₹2,630 respectively, Citi and Jefferies issued Sell and Underperform ratings citing margin pressures. Net profit grew 4% sequentially to ₹13,884 crore, though EBIT margins remained slightly below estimates at 24%.
items.title: TCS Shares Rise on Results Amid Mixed Analyst Outlook

items.summary: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy supported SpaceX founder Elon Musk regarding allegations that Starlink services were blocked in India by oligarchs. Reddy stated India could not afford to appease such distractions and highlighted the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) as a model of Indian innovation. Conversely, the Indian government denied the claims as baseless, asserting its regulatory framework is fair and non-discriminatory. Meanwhile, opposition leader Rahul Gandhi welcomed Musk to India, while Musk questioned why a license had not yet been granted, suggesting Ambani might be the real boss. The Ministry of Communications confirmed that security assessments for Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb, and Jio Satellite Communications are currently underway.
items.title: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy Defends Elon Musk Against Starlink Allegations

items.summary: Former Amazon Web Services employee Daniel Vassallo defended the role of immigrant workers in building major American technology companies, stating that the presence of foreign talent was instrumental to their growth. Vassallo, who worked at Amazon for over eight years, recalled that nearly everyone at the AWS organization he joined in Seattle was an immigrant, estimating the ratio was approximately 20:1. His comments come amid intensifying scrutiny of employment-based immigration programs by the Trump administration, which has suspended several major IT outsourcing companies and technology firms from the PERM program. Vice President JD Vance criticized the H-1B visa program, arguing it has become rife with fraud and should prioritize American workers.
items.title: Former AWS Employee Defends Immigrant Workforce Amid Visa Scrutiny

items.summary: Hexaware Technologies and Anthropic announced a multi-year partnership integrating Anthropic's Claude into Hexaware's AI platforms, Zerovity and AgentVerse. The deal designates Hexaware as a Preferred Partner to help enterprises deploy AI solutions at scale. Hexaware plans to utilize Claude for IT operations and software engineering, leveraging its existing pool of certified professionals to deliver business outcomes.
items.title: Hexaware and Anthropic Form Multi-Year AI Partnership

items.summary: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty rebounded in early trade following a two-day decline. The Sensex rose 292 points while Nifty gained 84.60 points, led by Tata Consultancy Services which surged over 4 per cent after reporting a 15 per cent jump in net profit to Rs 13,884 crore. Other IT stocks also gained, while foreign investors offloaded equities worth Rs 12,943.58 crore on Thursday.
items.title: Sensex and Nifty rebound as TCS profit jump drives rally

items.summary: President Donald Trump honored six tech billionaires, including Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, for their contributions to American innovation. However, Vice President JD Vance announced shortly after that Microsoft was suspended from a program allowing skilled foreign workers to apply for green cards via H-1B visas. Vance accused the company of abusing the visa system, citing that Microsoft fired 6,000 U.S. workers last year while obtaining 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. While Trump praised the honorees as 'national treasures,' Vance maintained support for Microsoft, stating the company must hire great American workers. The White House spokesperson noted the recipients help ensure America leads in innovation.
items.title: Trump Honors Tech Leaders While Vice President Accuses Microsoft of Visa Abuse

items.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs stated that suspending PERM applications does not affect existing H-1B visa validity but may impact the Green Card process. India argued that the U.S. steps do not advance shared ambitions and described Vice-President J.D. Vance's comments as unwarranted and offensive due to their historical connotations. The ministry emphasized that skilled professional mobility benefits both economies through innovation and productivity.
items.title: India rejects U.S. green card suspension as counterproductive to shared ambitions

items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved renaming the Noida International Airport at Jewar to 'Narendra Modi International Airport, Noida-Jewar' on October 9, 2026. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath stated the state expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the airport, describing it as a major gift and a future aviation hub. The Cabinet aims to realize a developed India by 2047.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Renames Jewar Airport After PM Modi

items.summary: The Supreme Court questioned why the Cockroach Janta Party did not challenge the Delhi Police's denial of permission for an October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar. Justice Joymalya Bagchi noted that protests without permission are unlawful. While the right to peaceful protest exists, the Court indicated it could ease restrictions if organizers challenged the denial and provided assurances regarding crowd size and public safety. The police cited short notice and past violations as reasons for the refusal.
items.title: Supreme Court Questions Protest Permission Denial Ahead of CJP Demonstration

items.summary: Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority reported that three Saudi nationals were killed and several injured in two attacks on King Khalid International Airport and a Saudia Airlines aircraft. While the authority did not identify the perpetrators, Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen claimed responsibility. Operations at the airport have resumed, and the Indian Embassy advised nationals to remain vigilant.
items.title: Houthi Attacks Kill Three at Riyadh Airport and Damage Saudia Plane

items.summary: Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling announced the suspension of major IT firms, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, Capgemini, Microsoft, and Adobe, from the permanent labor certification program. Sonderling alleged systemic fraud involving nearly 3 million foreign workers and over 230,000 H-1B approvals since 2009, claiming these actions protected American workers from job displacement.
items.title: Labor Secretary Suspends Major IT Firms Over Alleged Visa Fraud

items.summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has urged the Delhi government to ban large-scale protests in key commercial areas from Navratri to Diwali. CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal stated that repeated demonstrations disrupt metro services and deter shoppers, citing a 70% drop in business activity. The group also proposed a permanent protest zone outside central Delhi.
items.title: CTI Demands Protest Ban in Delhi Amid Business Disruption

items.summary: Cupid shares hit a fresh 52-week high of Rs 368, rising 3% for the fourth consecutive session. The stock has surged 657% over the past year. The company raised its FY27 guidance, expecting revenue of Rs 800 crore and net profit of Rs 250 crore, citing sustained momentum. It plans to scale distribution and operationalize a new manufacturing facility.
items.title: Cupid Shares Rally on Raised FY27 Guidance

items.summary: Repeated marine heatwaves are narrowing the window for coral reef recovery, raising the risk of long-term decline. Since 1998, every strong El Niño has coincided with global coral bleaching events. The UN Environment Programme warns reefs are hit by new bleaching events before recovering from earlier ones. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change warns that 70-90% of warm water coral reefs will disappear even if global warming is constrained to 1.5°C. Marine heatwaves are pushing corals beyond thermal stress thresholds. In India, a 24-year study recorded coral cover falling from about 37% to under 20% in Lakshadweep since 1998. Experts note that reefs need about six bleaching-free years to recover, a window becoming increasingly rare.
items.title: El Niño Strengthens, Coral Reefs Face Narrow Recovery Windows

items.summary: The Patna High Court has sought all records in a contempt case involving a former Rohtas district police chief after a trial court proceeded against him. The bench noted the procedural propriety issue as the original judgment faces challenge. Advocate General S D Sanjay argued the trial court could not direct an FIR for false evidence. The court ordered no further action until the final hearing.
items.title: Patna High Court Seeks Records in Rohtas Ex-SP Contempt Case

items.summary: Prachi Mishra, an economics professor at Ashoka University, argues that India and Japan must deepen trade and technology partnerships to strengthen supply chains, noting their current economic relationship remains small despite strategic cooperation. Mishra highlights significant untapped potential in semiconductors, rare earths, and investment. She points out that Japan's share in India's trade has dropped from over 10% in the 1980s to 1-2% today, while India's share in Japan's imports is less than 1%. Mishra suggests that closer cooperation could help both nations diversify supply chains and build resilience against global economic fragmentation.
items.title: Expert Calls for Deeper India-Japan Trade and Tech Ties

items.summary: Producer-actor Anjali Patil is in South Korea for the world premiere of her Tamil film Selvi at the 31st Busan International Film Festival on October 9. The film, revolving around a woman caregiver, explores themes often overlooked in mainstream cinema. Patil expresses her desire to shift the landscape of Indian cinema away from fear regarding women-centric stories. She believes audiences are intelligent and should be offered holistic, entertaining, and eye-opening content that celebrates female intelligence and power. Patil, who launched her production house Anahat Films in 2021, aims to create an ecosystem that defies gender, caste, and class hierarchies.
items.title: Anjali Patil Advocates for Women-Centric Films at Busan

items.summary: The All India N.R. Congress (AINRC) candidate Ashok Anand won the Thattanchavady bypoll in Puducherry with a margin of 8,482 votes, nearly double the previous Assembly election result. Anand secured 13,358 votes against rival E. Vinayagam's 4,876. The victory did not alter the National Democratic Alliance's majority in the 30-member Assembly.
items.title: AINRC Retains Thattanchavady Seat in Puducherry Bypoll

items.summary: Michael Dell defended updated federal regulations allowing donors to gift corporate shares into children's Trump Accounts, dismissing concerns about market manipulation. While critics warn of tying wealth to single entities, Dell argues it sparks interest in capitalism. The policy shift follows a transition to automatic enrollment for 70 million children, with Dell's $6.25 billion pledge already deployed to 10 million recipients.
items.title: Michael Dell Defends New Trump Account Rules

items.summary: The Delhi High Court stayed a government order mandating Aadhaar biometric attendance for public prosecutors in trial courts. Justice Amit Mahajan issued the stay following a petition by the Delhi Prosecutors' Welfare Association. Lawyers argued the order was arbitrary and violated privacy rights, noting that prosecutors' work is court-centric and involves pre-court duties. The court will hear the matter again in December.
items.title: Delhi High Court Stays Aadhaar Attendance Order for Prosecutors

items.summary: The GST Council met on October 8, 2026, to approve significant administrative reforms effective April 1, 2027. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman confirmed that tax rates were not discussed, focusing instead on procedural changes. Approved measures include a simplified registration system, faster refund processing, removal of arrest powers for officers, and new rules for service exports. The Council also announced a faceless assessment system for Central GST companies. Finance Minister Sitharaman stated that 99% of rate and process reforms are now complete, with remaining issues to be addressed incrementally.
items.title: GST Council Approves Major Administrative Reforms for 2027

items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved renaming Jewar Airport to Narendra Modi International Airport. Inaugurated in March 2026, the airport began operations in June. CM Yogi Adityanath thanked the Prime Minister, noting the facility's potential as a major aviation hub. The airport, built via a PPP model, has an initial capacity of about 12 million passengers, with plans to expand to 70 million.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Renames Jewar Airport for PM Modi
